legal_issues.issue: Which documents of title and which registry and survey records must be called for to establish that the vendor can convey a clear and marketable title to the land and the office building.
What must be called for to disclose encumbrances: registered instruments and lis pendens on the land registry folio, and charges registered against a corporate vendor with the Registrar of Companies.

What corporate documents are required on both sides so that the transfer is validly executed and is not prohibited, given that the purchaser is a company incorporated in Sri Lanka with foreign shareholders and the price may make the purchase a major transaction.

What planning, building and local authority documents must be called for in respect of an office building within a Municipality and a declared development area, including outstanding charges on the premises.

gold_answer_draft.issue: What documents should the purchaser's lawyer call for to examine title before Tea Exports (Private) Limited buys the ten perch property with the office building in Colombo, and what is the reason for each. Three groups arise: documents proving the seller's title and the extent of the land, documents disclosing encumbrances and claims, and documents dealing with the corporate capacity of the two companies and with the local authority and planning position of the building.
gold_answer_draft.rule: No sale or transfer of immovable property avails in law unless the deed is in writing, signed by the executants and the witnesses in the presence of a licensed notary and attested by him, and where the transferee is a corporate body whose board cannot attend, the board must authorise a signatory in writing (Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2(1)(a) and s.2(2)(a)). An unregistered instrument is void against a later instrument taken for valuable consideration and duly registered (Registration of Documents Ordinance s.7), registration counts only if made in the proper folio or a folio opened in continuation of it (s.14), a lis pendens does not bind a purchaser until registered (s.11), and any person interested, or his attorney-at-law, may search the books and obtain certified copies and extracts (s.42). Paper title is not conclusive, because ten years of undisturbed and uninterrupted adverse possession founds a title (Prescription Ordinance s.3). An instrument that is not duly stamped may not be registered or acted upon (Western Province Financial Statute s.60), and a plan is receivable in evidence only if prepared or certified as the Survey Act s.13 requires. Where a company creates a charge on land it must deliver the instrument to the Registrar for registration (Companies Act s.102), and registration is notice of the particulars of the charge to all persons (s.105). A certificate of incorporation is conclusive evidence of incorporation (s.5), and a company may not enter into a major transaction, which includes acquiring assets worth more than half the value of its assets before the acquisition, except by special resolution, unanimous written shareholder consent or express authority in its articles (s.185). Transfer of land to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka is prohibited where direct or indirect foreign shareholding is fifty per cent or above, unless an exemption in s.3 applies (Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act s.2). A building in a Municipality may not be occupied until the Council certifies conformity (Municipal Councils Ordinance s.127), council expenses of the kind described are a first charge on the premises payable by successors in title (s.152), development activity in a declared development area requires a permit (Urban Development Authority Law s.8J), and land may be under notice of intended acquisition given to the owner (Land Acquisition Act s.4). Where land lies in an area declared under the Registration of Title Act s.1, the Certificate of Title under s.37 replaces the deed chain, and a registered power of attorney is required for a deed signed by an attorney (Powers of Attorney Ordinance s.3).
gold_answer_draft.application: Since the land is on a deeds folio in Colombo and not in a declared title registration area, the deed chain governs. The seller has produced only three instruments, the latest being Deed of Transfer No. 3128 of 2012 and the earliest Deed of Gift No. 812 of 1986; earlier deeds, or their registered duplicates or certified registry copies, must be called for so that the chain runs back well beyond any period in which a possessory title could have been perfected, and each deed must be inspected for the notarial attestation and for the stamp or endorsement of payment. A certified extract of the land registry folio and of every folio connected to it by cross reference must be called for, because that alone will show the mortgage bond of 2019, any other registered instrument taking priority, and any registered lis pendens. Because Deed No. 1476 of 1994 was signed by an attorney, the power of attorney, its registration particulars and evidence that it was unrevoked at that date must be produced. Plan No. 4372 of 2011 and a certified copy must be called for and, since the boundaries have not been checked on the ground, a fresh survey by a registered licensed surveyor is prudent to confirm that the ten perches match the description in the deeds and that the building stands within the boundaries. Possession must be proved independently of the deeds by rates and assessment receipts, utility bills and the tenancy or lease records for the office building. Because the seller is a company, certified copies of its certificate of incorporation, articles, directors' particulars and the resolution authorising the sale must be called for, a search made of the Registrar's register of charges, and the certificate of registration of the 2019 charge, the mortgage bond and the bank's letter agreeing to release the mortgage on payment obtained. On the purchaser's side, the certificate of incorporation, the articles, the share register and the latest annual return must be produced to show that direct and indirect foreign shareholding stands at thirty-five per cent and so below the prohibited level, and since the price of Rs. 480 million exceeds half the value of the company's assets, the special resolution or written consent of all shareholders approving the acquisition, together with the written board authority for the signatory to the transfer, must be in hand before execution. As the building was put up in 2013 within the Municipality and a declared development area, the approved building plan, the development permit and the certificate of conformity must be called for, along with a council statement of rates and other charges, which will disclose the unpaid drainage works expenses and the gap in rates receipts after 2021, and confirmation about street lines and building limits. Confirmation must also be obtained that no notice of intended acquisition affects the land, since none has been produced.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The purchaser's lawyer should call for, and give the following reasons for: the seller's deed and the prior deeds or their registered duplicates and certified registry copies, going back far enough to exclude a possessory claim, because only a notarially executed and duly registered chain gives priority; a certified extract of the land registry folio and connected folios, covering registered instruments and lis pendens, because registration decides priority and a registered pending action binds a purchaser; the power of attorney for the 1994 deed; the survey plan, a certified copy and if necessary a fresh survey, because only a properly certified plan is receivable in evidence and the extent must match the deeds; possessory documents, being rates receipts, utility bills and tenancy records, because ten years of adverse possession can defeat a paper title; stamp endorsements and receipts on every deed, because an unstamped instrument cannot be registered or acted upon; the seller company's certificate of incorporation, articles, directors' particulars and authorising resolution, a search of the Registrar's register of charges and the release of the registered mortgage, because registration of a charge is notice to all persons; the purchaser company's certificate of incorporation, articles, share register and annual return, because a transfer to a company with fifty per cent or more foreign shareholding is prohibited, together with the special resolution or unanimous written shareholder consent for what is a major transaction and the written board authority for the signatory; and the approved building plan, development permit, certificate of conformity, council rates and charges statement, street line and building limit confirmation, and confirmation that no acquisition proceeding affects the land. Title should not be accepted until the outstanding council expenses are settled or retained from the price and the mortgage is released on completion.

answer_claims.claim_text: A sale or transfer of immovable property does not avail in law unless the deed is in writing, signed by every executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licensed notary and attested by him, so every link in the chain produced must be a notarially executed deed.

An instrument that is not duly registered is void against a subsequent instrument taken for valuable consideration and duly registered, so the deeds must be checked against what is actually registered on the folio.

A person interested in the land, or his attorney-at-law, may search the registry books and indexes and obtain certified copies and extracts, which is the authority for calling for a certified folio extract and for certified copies of registered duplicates of missing deeds.

Registration is effective only in the folio in which the first registered instrument affecting the land was registered or in a folio opened in continuation of it with cross references, so the extract called for must cover every connected folio.
A registered lis pendens binds a purchaser for valuable consideration, so the search must extend to registered pending actions and particulars of any disclosed action must be called for.
Ten years of undisturbed and uninterrupted possession adverse to the paper owner founds a title, so documents evidencing possession must be called for in addition to the deeds.

An instrument chargeable with stamp duty may not be registered or acted upon unless duly stamped, so each deed must carry the stamp or the endorsement of payment and the receipts must be produced with it.

A plan or map is receivable in evidence only if prepared or certified by the Surveyor-General, an authorised registered surveyor or a registered licensed surveyor, so the plan called for must satisfy that requirement.

A charge on land created by a company must be delivered to the Registrar for registration, and registration is notice to all persons of the particulars of the charge, so a search of the register of charges is required where the seller is a company.

A certificate of incorporation is conclusive evidence that the company was incorporated and that the incorporation requirements were met, which is why it and the articles and current directors' particulars are called for from each company.

A company may not enter into a major transaction, which includes acquiring assets worth more than half the value of its assets before the acquisition, unless it is approved by special resolution, consented to in writing by all shareholders or expressly authorised by its articles.
Transfer of land to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka is prohibited where direct or indirect foreign shareholding is fifty per cent or above, unless one of the statutory exemptions applies.
Where the transferee is a corporate body whose board cannot attend to execute the deed, the board must authorise a signatory in writing, so that written authority must be obtained before execution.

A building in a Municipality may not be occupied until the Council certifies that it conforms to the Ordinance and the by-laws, and development activity in a declared development area requires a permit, so the approved plan, permit and certificate of conformity are called for.

Council expenses of the kind described rank with the rates as a first charge on the premises and are payable by the owner and his successors in title, so a council statement of rates and charges must be called for.
A power of attorney must be registered with the Registrar-General, so where a deed in the chain was signed by an attorney the power and its registration particulars must be produced.
Land may be under a notice of intended acquisition given to the owner, so the purchaser must call for any such notice and for confirmation that no acquisition proceeding affects the land.

Title registration applies only to areas declared by Order, and in a declared area the Certificate of Title is the document to be called for; since this land remains on a deeds folio, the deed chain and folio extract govern.

Because the seller has produced only the 2012, 1994 and 1986 instruments, the earlier deeds or their registered duplicates or certified registry copies must be called for so that the chain runs back beyond any period in which a possessory title could have matured.

A certified extract of the Colombo land registry folio and of every folio connected to it must be called for, since that is what will disclose the 2019 mortgage bond, any competing registered instrument and any registered lis pendens.
Because the 1994 deed was signed by an attorney, the power of attorney, its registration particulars and evidence that it was unrevoked at that date must be produced before that link is accepted.

Plan No. 4372 of 2011 and a certified copy must be called for, and because the boundaries have not been checked on the ground a fresh survey by a registered licensed surveyor should be obtained to confirm that the ten perches and the building match the description in the deeds.

Since the seller is a company that filed particulars of the 2019 mortgage with the Registrar of Companies, its certificate of incorporation, articles, directors' particulars and authorising resolution must be called for, a search made of the register of charges, and the bank's release of the mortgage obtained on completion.

The purchaser's share register and latest annual return must be produced to establish that direct and indirect foreign shareholding stands at thirty-five per cent, below the level at which a transfer to the company would be prohibited.

Because the price of Rs. 480 million exceeds half the value of the purchaser's assets before the acquisition, a certified special resolution or the written consent of all its shareholders, together with the articles and the written board authority for the signatory, must be in hand before the transfer is executed.

As the building was put up in 2013 within the Municipality and a declared development area, the approved building plan, the development permit and the certificate of conformity must be called for, and the council statement will disclose the unpaid drainage works expenses and the gap in rates receipts after 2021.
Since nothing has been produced about any intended State acquisition, confirmation must be obtained from the acquiring officer that no acquisition proceeding affects the land.

The documents to be called for are the chain of notarially executed deeds with their registration and stamp endorsements, a certified folio extract covering registered instruments and lis pendens, the power of attorney for the 1994 deed, the survey plan and if necessary a fresh survey, possessory documents such as rates receipts, utility bills and tenancy records, the corporate documents and charge search for the seller company with the release of the mortgage, the purchaser company's incorporation, shareholding and resolution documents with the written board authority, and the building plan, development permit, certificate of conformity, council rates and charges statement, street line confirmation and confirmation that no acquisition affects the land.

Title should not be accepted, and the price should not be paid over, until the outstanding council expenses are settled or retained and the registered mortgage is released on completion, because both would otherwise bind the company as successor in title.

enrichment.original_background: The said Tea Exports (Private) Limited needs to purchase an office building situated in Colombo. Ten Perches (AO, RO, P10) in extent.
enrichment.enriched_background: Tea Exports (Private) Limited, a company incorporated in Sri Lanka, needs to purchase an office building situated in Colombo, ten perches (A0, R0, P10) in extent. The premises are Assessment No. 118, Sir James Peiris Mawatha, Colombo 02, within the administrative limits of the Colombo Municipal Council and within a declared development area; the building was put up in 2013. The land is depicted as Lot 1 in Plan No. 4372 dated 12 August 2011 made by a registered licensed surveyor, and the boundaries have not been checked on the ground since. The seller is Galle Face Holdings (Private) Limited, a company incorporated in Sri Lanka, which is in possession and holds the premises as registered proprietor. Its own title is under Deed of Transfer No. 3128 attested on 4 February 2012 by a notary practising in Colombo; the only earlier instruments produced so far are Deed of Transfer No. 1476 of 1994 and Deed of Gift No. 812 of 1986, and nothing before 1986 has been shown. Deed No. 1476 of 1994 was signed for the then owner by an attorney and not by the owner himself. The premises are mortgaged to a licensed commercial bank under Mortgage Bond No. 2205 of 2019, and the seller filed particulars of that mortgage with the Registrar of Companies. Two of the five shareholders of Tea Exports (Private) Limited are foreign nationals who hold thirty-five per cent of the issued shares between them, and the agreed price of Rs. 480 million is more than half the value of the assets of Tea Exports (Private) Limited before the acquisition. The Council carried out drainage improvement works on the premises in 2022, part of the recoverable cost is still unpaid, and rates receipts have been produced only up to 2021. The land registry for Colombo keeps the land on a deeds folio, and no order has been produced bringing it under the title registration system. Completion is intended for October 2024, and the seller has produced nothing about any intended acquisition of the land by the State.

added_facts.fact: The seller is Galle Face Holdings (Private) Limited, a company incorporated in Sri Lanka, which is in possession and holds the premises as registered proprietor.
added_facts.reason: The original scenario names only the purchaser. Whether the seller is an individual or a company decides whether the company registers and the corporate execution documents come into the title examination at all.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If the seller were an individual, the certificate of incorporation, articles, directors' particulars and the search of the Registrar's register of charges would fall away and the encumbrance search would rest on the land registry folio alone.

added_facts.fact: The premises are Assessment No. 118, Sir James Peiris Mawatha, Colombo 02, within the administrative limits of the Colombo Municipal Council and within a declared development area, and the building was put up in 2013.
added_facts.reason: The original background says only that the building is in Colombo. Identifying the local authority and the declared development area, and dating the building, is what makes the local authority and planning documents necessary.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If the premises were outside a Municipality and outside a declared development area, the certificate of conformity and the development permit would not be called for and the local authority search would be against a different authority.

added_facts.fact: The land is depicted as Lot 1 in Plan No. 4372 dated 12 August 2011 made by a registered licensed surveyor, and the boundaries have not been checked on the ground since.
added_facts.reason: Ten perches has to be tied to a described lot for the extent stated in the deeds to be verifiable. The plan gives the scenario a determinate description without deciding any issue.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If no plan existed, a fresh survey by a registered licensed surveyor would be the document called for instead of the existing plan and its certified copy.

added_facts.fact: The seller's title is under Deed of Transfer No. 3128 attested on 4 February 2012 by a notary practising in Colombo; the only earlier instruments produced are Deed of Transfer No. 1476 of 1994 and Deed of Gift No. 812 of 1986, and nothing before 1986 has been shown.
added_facts.reason: The original scenario gives no chain at all. A determinate chain with a stated stopping point is what makes the demand for earlier deeds, registered duplicates and certified copies concrete.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If the seller produced an unbroken set of notarially attested deeds with registration endorsements over a longer period, the demand would be limited to the folio extract and the possessory documents.

added_facts.fact: Deed No. 1476 of 1994 was signed for the then owner by an attorney and not by the owner himself.
added_facts.reason: A link executed under a power of attorney adds a document to the list that would otherwise not be called for, and creates a specific risk in the chain.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If every deed had been signed by the owner personally, the power of attorney, its registration particulars and evidence that it was unrevoked would not be called for.

added_facts.fact: The premises are mortgaged to a licensed commercial bank under Mortgage Bond No. 2205 of 2019, and the seller filed particulars of that mortgage with the Registrar of Companies.
added_facts.reason: The candidate record flags a missing encumbrance. A subsisting registered mortgage granted by a corporate seller is what makes both the folio extract and the company charge search operative rather than formal.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If the premises were unencumbered, the searches would still be made, but no release of mortgage and no certificate of registration of a charge would have to be produced at completion.

added_facts.fact: Two of the five shareholders of Tea Exports (Private) Limited are foreign nationals who hold thirty-five per cent of the issued shares between them.
added_facts.reason: The scenario says only that the purchaser is a private limited company. Whether foreign shareholding reaches fifty per cent decides whether the transfer is prohibited outright, so the shareholding documents belong in the list.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If direct or indirect foreign shareholding were fifty per cent or above and no exemption applied, the transfer would be prohibited and the purchase could not proceed in this form.

added_facts.fact: The agreed price is Rs. 480 million, which is more than half the value of the assets of Tea Exports (Private) Limited before the acquisition.
added_facts.reason: The size of the acquisition relative to the company's assets is what turns the purchase into a major transaction and puts the shareholders' resolution on the list of documents.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If the price were well below half the value of the company's assets, a directors' resolution and the articles would suffice and no special resolution or unanimous shareholder consent would be called for.

added_facts.fact: The Council carried out drainage improvement works on the premises in 2022, part of the recoverable cost is still unpaid, and rates receipts have been produced only up to 2021.
added_facts.reason: An outstanding council charge that runs with the premises is what makes the rates and council clearance documents decisive rather than routine.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If rates and council expenses were paid up to date, the council statement would be a formality and no adjustment or retention from the price would be needed.

added_facts.fact: The land registry for Colombo keeps the land on a deeds folio, and no order has been produced bringing it under the title registration system.
added_facts.reason: Fixes which registration system governs, so the answer can rest on the deed chain and the folio extract rather than on a certificate of title.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If the land were in a declared area under the title registration system, the certificate of title would be the document called for and the deed chain would drop back to a secondary role.

added_facts.fact: Completion is intended for October 2024, and the seller has produced nothing about any intended acquisition of the land by the State.
added_facts.reason: Fixes the date at which the law is applied and makes explicit that no acquisition clearance is yet in hand.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If a notice of intended acquisition had been served on the seller, the purchase would have to be reconsidered rather than merely documented.

block_reason: Verifier downgrade. Three claims in the gold answer do not stand as written, and the verifier may not rewrite the answer prose. (1) CL-M030-Q01-021 is rejected: section 11(1) of Act, No. 38 of 2014 bars mortgaging only land transferred or leased to a person or company referred to in section 2(1) or 5(1), so the five-year bar does not reach the corporate route with foreign shareholding below fifty per cent, yet the claim and the application paragraph state that it applies whichever route the client takes. (2) CL-M030-Q01-020 is disputed: the voidness of a transfer to a local company whose foreign shareholding later reaches fifty per cent comes from section 2(2)(b), which is not in the map, and it is subject to provisos allowing the breach to be cured within twelve months (listed company) or six months (any other). (3) CL-M030-Q01-022 is disputed: no provision in this corpus obliges a notary to decline to draw or attest an instrument void under another Act, so the notarial-refusal limb of the conclusion rests on professional duty rather than on cited statute. The rest of the map is verified; a lawyer should adjudicate these three points.

indispensable_provisions.formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
indispensable_provisions.relevant_excerpt: Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary in any other written law, the transfer of title of any land situated in Sri Lanka, shall be prohibited if such transfer is- (a) to a foreigner; or (b) to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka under the Companies Act where any foreign shareholding in such company, either direct or indirect, is fifty per cent or above; or (c) to a foreign company, unless exempted as provided in section 3.
indispensable_provisions.why_relevant: This is the operative prohibition. It bars the very transaction the client proposes - the transfer of title of private land in Sri Lanka to a person who is not a citizen - and it is the provision on which the whole advice turns. It also fixes the alternative transferee route (a Sri Lankan company with less than fifty per cent foreign shareholding) and points to the section 3 exemptions.
indispensable_provisions.temporal_note: Section 2 has been in force since the Act commenced in 2014 and carries no amendment event in the corpus consolidation, so the text applies at the matter reference date of October 2024.

indispensable_provisions.formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
indispensable_provisions.relevant_excerpt: means a person who is not a citizen of Sri Lanka; means a company or a body of persons incorporated under the laws of any country other than Sri Lanka;
indispensable_provisions.why_relevant: The prohibition in section 2 operates on the defined term 'foreigner'. The definition is purely negative - anyone who is not a citizen of Sri Lanka - so the client's nationality, and not his residence, visa status or business purpose, decides whether section 2 catches him. Without this definition the prohibition cannot be applied to him.
indispensable_provisions.temporal_note: Section 25 has been in force since 2014 with no amendment event recorded in the corpus, so it applies at October 2024. Caveat for the verifier: in the corpus text of section 25 the defined terms themselves have been dropped in extraction, so the excerpt reads as two bare 'means ...' clauses; in the printed Act these are the definitions of 'foreigner' and 'foreign company' respectively.
indispensable_provisions.verifier_note: Verified: the corpus metadata for 38-2014/s25 lists twenty defined terms in the same order as the twenty 'means/includes' clauses in the body, and the ninth and tenth clauses are 'foreigner' and 'foreign company', so the label loss noted by the researcher does not affect the mapping.

indispensable_provisions.formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
indispensable_provisions.relevant_excerpt: means any State or private land and includes- (a) any interest in the land; (b) any land covered with water; and (c) any house or building stands on that land; means the Minister to whom the subject of Finance has been assigned; means any sale, donation, gift or any conveyance by or under which the title of such land passes to another person;
indispensable_provisions.why_relevant: The two other defined terms the prohibition depends on. 'Land' covers private as well as State land and extends to any interest in the land and to buildings on it, so a private bare-land purchase for an apartment development is within the Act. 'Transfer' covers any sale or conveyance passing title, which is exactly the deed the client wants attested.
indispensable_provisions.temporal_note: Same section and same commencement as PROV-M030-002; in force at October 2024. The extraction has again dropped the term labels, so the excerpt runs the definitions of 'land', 'Minister' and 'transfer' together.
indispensable_provisions.verifier_note: Verified on the same clause-to-term alignment as PROV-M030-002: clauses fifteen, sixteen and seventeen of 38-2014/s25 are 'land', 'Minister' and 'transfer'.

indispensable_provisions.formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
indispensable_provisions.relevant_excerpt: (1) The provisions of section 2 shall not apply to- (a) any land the title of which is transferred to a Diplomatic Mission of another State within the meaning of the Diplomatic Privileges Act or to an International, Multilateral or Bilateral Organization recognized in terms of that Act; (b) a condominium parcel specified under the Apartment Ownership Law: Provided that, the entire value shall be paid upfront through an inward foreign remittance prior to the execution of the relevant deed of transfer;
indispensable_provisions.why_relevant: The exception the advice must be checked against. Paragraph (b) is the one route by which a foreigner may take freehold title in an apartment context - a condominium parcel under the Apartment Ownership Law, and then only if the entire value is remitted from abroad before the deed is executed. The remaining paragraphs (dual citizens, next of kin, banks, listed companies) are the exhaustive list against which the client's position must be tested before advising that section 2 bites.
indispensable_provisions.temporal_note: Section 3(1) was amended by the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) (Amendment) Act, No. 21 of 2018, section 2, which substituted paragraph (b) and added paragraph (i). The corpus text is the consolidated post-2018 text, which is the text in force at October 2024. The verifier should note that the corpus body of 21-2018 section 2 is truncated and does not itself show the substituted paragraph (b).

indispensable_provisions.formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
indispensable_provisions.relevant_excerpt: Any alienation of land effected in contravention of the provisions of this Act, shall be void and shall have no effect in law.
indispensable_provisions.why_relevant: The consequence that makes the advice urgent. A deed of transfer taken in the teeth of section 2 is not merely unregistrable; it is void, so the client would pay the price and acquire nothing. This is what the attorney and notary must tell the client before any deed is drawn.
indispensable_provisions.temporal_note: In force from 2014 and unamended in the corpus consolidation; applies at October 2024.

indispensable_provisions.relevant_excerpt: (4) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other law but subject to the provisions of this Law, after the registration of a Condominium Plan, or Semi Condominium Plan, any condominium parcel depicted therein together with the common elements appurtenant thereto may be held and dealt with in the same manner and form as any land.
indispensable_provisions.why_relevant: Explains what the condominium exemption in section 3(1)(b) of the 2014 Act actually gives a foreign buyer: once a Condominium Plan is registered, each condominium parcel with its share of the common elements may be held and dealt with as land. It also shows why the exemption does not help a purchase of bare land over which no Condominium Plan has been registered.
indispensable_provisions.temporal_note: Section 9 has been in force since 1973 and was last amended in 2003, before the matter reference date of October 2024.
indispensable_provisions.verifier_note: Verified; role raised from supporting to indispensable, because ruling out the section 3(1)(b) condominium exemption is a necessary step in the answer rather than a supporting one.

indispensable_provisions.relevant_excerpt: means a defined space which is shown as an independent parcel on a condominium plan or semi condominium plan or provisional condominium plan and which is designed for independent use consisting of one or more rooms whether occupying the entirety or part of one or more storeys in a building of more than one storey and which is shown as a separate condominium parcel
indispensable_provisions.why_relevant: The exemption in section 3(1)(b) of Act, No. 38 of 2014 is expressed in the term 'condominium parcel specified under the Apartment Ownership Law', and this is the definition of that term. It is what makes the exclusion of bare land determinate: a condominium parcel is a defined space shown as an independent parcel on a condominium plan, semi condominium plan or provisional condominium plan, so an allotment of bare land over which no such plan has been registered cannot be a condominium parcel and the exemption cannot be reached.
indispensable_provisions.temporal_note: Section 26 is the interpretation section of the Apartment Ownership Law; the corpus records it as in force from 1973 with its latest change in 2003, both before the matter reference date of October 2024.
indispensable_provisions.verifier_note: Added by the verifier. The research notes rejected 11-1973 s.26 as garbled, but the clause the researcher read as the definition of 'condominium parcel' ('a parcel intended for separate ownership...') is in fact the definition of 'accessory parcel'; the corpus defined-term order places 'condominium parcel' immediately after 'Condominium Plan', and that clause is clean and verbatim.

supporting_provisions.formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
supporting_provisions.relevant_excerpt: (a) For the purpose of maintaining the legal validity of a transfer of land to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka under the Companies Act, with less than fifty per cent of foreign shareholding, the foreign shareholding of such company shall remain less than fifty per cent, for a minimum period of consecutive twenty (20) years from the date of such transfer.
supporting_provisions.why_relevant: Qualifies the corporate route. If the client is advised to acquire through a Sri Lankan company, the sub-fifty per cent foreign shareholding is not a one-off test at the date of the deed; it must be held for twenty consecutive years, failing which the transfer becomes void. This is the most important warning to give a client who is told he may buy through a local company.
supporting_provisions.temporal_note: Part of section 2, in force from 2014, unamended in the corpus consolidation; applies at October 2024.
supporting_provisions.verifier_note: Wording is verbatim, but two corrections: the corpus body of 38-2014/s2 carries no '(2)' subsection marker before this paragraph, and the voidness consequence relied on in why_relevant sits in paragraph (b), not paragraph (a), and is subject to provisos allowing a company to cure a breach within twelve months (listed) or six months (unlisted); no excerpt of paragraph (b) is in the map.

supporting_provisions.formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
supporting_provisions.relevant_excerpt: Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary in any other written law, the leasing of a land- (a) to a foreigner; or (b) to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka under the Companies Act, where any foreign shareholding in such company, either direct or indirect, is fifty per cent or above; or (c) to a foreign company, shall be effected subject to the payment of the Land Lease Tax imposed under section 6: Provided however, the maximum tenure of any such lease shall not exceed ninety nine years.
supporting_provisions.why_relevant: The principal lawful alternative. A foreigner who cannot take title may take a lease, capped at ninety-nine years, which is long enough to support an apartment development. This is the constructive half of the advice.
supporting_provisions.temporal_note: In force from 2014 and unamended in the corpus consolidation, but it must be read with section 5A, which has since removed the Land Lease Tax from leases executed on or after 1 January 2016.

supporting_provisions.formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
supporting_provisions.relevant_excerpt: the provisions relating to the Land Lease Tax shall not apply to a lease of any land- (a) to a foreigner; or (b) to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka under the Companies Act, where any foreign shareholding in such company, either direct or indirect, is fifty per cent or above; or (c) to a foreign company, under and indenture of lease executed on or after January 1, 2016
supporting_provisions.why_relevant: Removes the cost objection to the lease route. The Land Lease Tax referred to in section 5(1) is not charged on an indenture of lease executed on or after 1 January 2016, so a lease taken in 2024 attracts no Land Lease Tax.
supporting_provisions.temporal_note: Section 5A was inserted by the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) (Amendment) Act, No. 3 of 2017, section 2 and further amended by Act, No. 21 of 2018, section 3. It is in force from 2017, before the matter reference date of October 2024, and it operates on leases executed on or after 1 January 2016.
supporting_provisions.verifier_note: Verified including the temporal chain: section 5A was inserted by 3-2017 s.2 with effect from January 8, 2017 and that date was substituted by 21-2018 s.3 with January 1, 2016, so the corpus text is the text in force at October 2024.

supporting_provisions.formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
supporting_provisions.relevant_excerpt: The Registrar of Lands shall not register an instrument effecting any transfer of title referred to in section 2, under the provisions of the Registration of Documents Ordinance, unless such registrar of lands is satisfied that such transfer is in compliance with the provisions of this Act.
supporting_provisions.why_relevant: The practical bar at the registry. Even if a deed were executed, the Registrar of Lands must refuse registration unless satisfied that the transfer complies with the Act, so the client would also be left with an unregistrable instrument.
supporting_provisions.temporal_note: In force from 2014 and unamended in the corpus consolidation; applies at October 2024.

supporting_provisions.formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
supporting_provisions.relevant_excerpt: Any land transferred or leased to a person or a company referred to in section 2(1) or 5(1), after the date on which the certificate of the speaker is endorsed in respect of this Act, shall not for any purpose be been mortgaged or pledged to any bank licensed under the Banking Act
supporting_provisions.why_relevant: A funding constraint the client must be warned about if he takes the lease route or acquires through a company with fifty per cent or more foreign shareholding: the land cannot be mortgaged or pledged to a licensed bank for five years from execution of the instrument, which matters to an apartment developer relying on construction finance.
supporting_provisions.temporal_note: In force from 2014 and unamended in the corpus consolidation; applies at October 2024. The corpus body of this section is visibly corrupted by extraction ('shall not for any purpose be been mortgaged ... for leased to a foreign a period of five years'); the excerpt has been kept short and the five-year period should be confirmed against the printed Act.
supporting_provisions.verifier_note: The five-year bar and its running from execution of the instrument are legible in the corrupted corpus body and the excerpt is verbatim, but the role is narrower than why_relevant states: section 11(1) bites only on land transferred or leased to a person or company 'referred to in section 2(1) or 5(1)', which does not include a Sri Lankan company whose foreign shareholding is below fifty per cent, so the bar does not reach the corporate route the map recommends.

supporting_provisions.formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
supporting_provisions.relevant_excerpt: (2) The Minister may in consultation with the Minister to whom the subject of lands has been assigned and with the prior written approval of the Cabinet of Ministers, by Order published in the Gazette, exempt any foreign entity engaged in the banking, financial, insurance, maritime, aviation, advanced technology or infrastructure development project identified as a Strategic Development Project, in terms of the provisions of the Strategic Development Projects Act, No. 14 of 2008, from the application of the provisions of section 2.
supporting_provisions.why_relevant: The discretionary exemption route. It is worth putting to the client, but it is confined to listed sectors and to a project identified as a Strategic Development Project, and it requires a Ministerial Order in the Gazette with prior Cabinet approval, so an ordinary private apartment venture cannot rely on it.
supporting_provisions.temporal_note: Subsection (2) was not touched by the 2018 amendment, which amended subsection (1) only; in force at October 2024.
supporting_provisions.verifier_note: Verified; note that section 3 also carries a third Ministerial exemption, in subsection (3), for a foreign company engaged in international commercial operations, which the map does not record.

legal_issues.issue: Whether a person who is not a citizen of Sri Lanka may take a transfer of title to private land in Sri Lanka.
Whether any statutory exemption, in particular the condominium parcel exemption or a Ministerial exemption for a Strategic Development Project, is available on these facts.
What the legal effect is of a deed of transfer executed in contravention of the prohibition, and what the Registrar of Lands must do with it.
What lawful alternatives (a lease of up to ninety-nine years, or acquisition through a Sri Lankan company with foreign shareholding below fifty per cent) are open, and on what conditions.
Whether the land so acquired or leased can be mortgaged to a licensed bank to fund the apartment construction.

gold_answer_draft.issue: Whether an Attorney-at-Law and Notary may lawfully draw and attest a deed transferring the freehold title of a private allotment of bare land in Dehiwala to a Swedish citizen who intends to develop and run an apartment business on it; if not, what consequences follow for such a deed and what lawful routes remain open to the client at October 2024.
gold_answer_draft.rule: Section 2(1) of the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014 prohibits the transfer of title of any land situated in Sri Lanka to a foreigner, to a Sri Lankan company in which direct or indirect foreign shareholding is fifty per cent or above, or to a foreign company, unless exempted under section 3. Section 25 defines a foreigner as a person who is not a citizen of Sri Lanka, defines land to include State and private land and any interest in it, and defines transfer as any sale or conveyance by which title passes. Section 3(1) lists the exemptions, of which the only one relevant to an apartment business is section 3(1)(b), a condominium parcel specified under the Apartment Ownership Law where the entire value is paid upfront by inward foreign remittance before the deed is executed; section 3(2) allows the Minister, with prior Cabinet approval, to exempt a foreign entity in listed sectors engaged in a Strategic Development Project. Under section 9(4) of the Apartment Ownership Law, No. 11 of 1973 a condominium parcel may be held and dealt with as land only after a Condominium Plan is registered. Section 18 of the 2014 Act makes any alienation in contravention of the Act void, and section 4(1) forbids the Registrar of Lands to register such a transfer. The lawful alternatives are a lease under section 5(1), which may not exceed ninety-nine years and on which, by section 5A, no Land Lease Tax is charged for an indenture executed on or after 1 January 2016, or acquisition through a company incorporated in Sri Lanka with less than fifty per cent foreign shareholding, which by section 2(2)(a) must stay below fifty per cent for twenty consecutive years. Section 11(1) bars mortgaging or pledging such land to a licensed bank for five years from execution of the instrument.
gold_answer_draft.application: Mr. Holmqvist is not a citizen of Sri Lanka and has no dual citizenship, so he is a foreigner within section 25 and the prohibition in section 2(1)(a) applies to him. The subject matter is a 38.5 perch allotment of private land at Hill Street, Dehiwala, which is land within section 25, and the proposed deed of transfer for Rs. 240,000,000 is a transfer within that section. None of the section 3(1) exemptions is available on these facts: he is not a diplomatic mission or an international organisation, not a dual citizen, not the next of kin of the owner, not a bank or a finance leasing institution, and the land is bare land over which no condominium plan has been registered, so there is no condominium parcel he could buy under section 3(1)(b). His willingness to remit the whole price from Stockholm does not assist, because that condition attaches only to the condominium exemption. He holds no Ministerial Order under section 3(2) and his venture has not been identified as a Strategic Development Project. A deed executed in October 2024 in his own name would therefore be void under section 18, and the Registrar of Lands would be bound by section 4(1) to refuse registration, so he would part with the price and acquire nothing. Because he is willing to restructure, two routes remain: a lease of the land to him for a term not exceeding ninety-nine years under section 5(1), on which no Land Lease Tax is payable because the indenture would be executed after 1 January 2016; or incorporation of a Sri Lankan company in which his shareholding stays below fifty per cent, subject to the twenty-year holding condition in section 2(2)(a), breach of which would render the transfer void. On his question about construction finance, section 11(1) prevents the land from being mortgaged or pledged to a licensed bank for five years from the execution of the transfer or lease. If instead his object is to own completed apartments rather than to develop the site, he could buy condominium parcels in a project whose Condominium Plan is already registered, paying the entire value upfront by inward foreign remittance before execution.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: He must be advised that he cannot buy this land in his own name: a deed of transfer to him would be void under section 18 of Act, No. 38 of 2014 and would not be registered. As his Notary you should decline to draw or attest such a deed. He should be advised instead to take a lease of the land for a term not exceeding ninety-nine years, on which no Land Lease Tax is now chargeable, or to acquire through a company incorporated in Sri Lanka whose foreign shareholding is and remains below fifty per cent for twenty years, or, if what he wants is completed apartments, to purchase registered condominium parcels with the entire value remitted from abroad before execution. He should also be warned that the land cannot be mortgaged to a licensed bank for five years, which affects his construction funding.

answer_claims.claim_text: Section 2(1)(a) of the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014 prohibits the transfer of title of any land situated in Sri Lanka to a foreigner, unless exempted under section 3.
For the purposes of that Act a foreigner is a person who is not a citizen of Sri Lanka.
Land includes private as well as State land and any interest in it, and transfer means any sale or conveyance by which title passes to another person.

The exemptions from section 2 are those set out in section 3(1), which include a condominium parcel specified under the Apartment Ownership Law where the entire value is paid upfront by inward foreign remittance before the deed of transfer is executed.

A condominium parcel may be held and dealt with in the same manner as land only after a Condominium Plan or Semi Condominium Plan has been registered under the Apartment Ownership Law, No. 11 of 1973.
The Minister may, with prior Cabinet approval and by Order published in the Gazette, exempt a foreign entity in the listed sectors engaged in a project identified as a Strategic Development Project.
Any alienation of land effected in contravention of the Act is void and of no effect in law.
The Registrar of Lands must refuse to register an instrument effecting a transfer referred to in section 2 unless satisfied that it complies with the Act.
A land may lawfully be leased to a foreigner, subject to the Land Lease Tax under section 6, for a maximum tenure of ninety-nine years.
No Land Lease Tax is charged, levied or collected on a lease to a foreigner under an indenture of lease executed on or after 1 January 2016.

Where land is transferred to a Sri Lankan company with less than fifty per cent foreign shareholding, that shareholding must remain below fifty per cent for twenty consecutive years from the date of transfer for the transfer to remain valid.
Land transferred or leased to a person or company referred to in section 2(1) or 5(1) may not be mortgaged or pledged to a licensed bank for five years from execution of the instrument.
Mr. Holmqvist, being a Swedish citizen who has never been a citizen of Sri Lanka and holds no dual citizenship, is a foreigner for the purposes of the Act.

The proposed acquisition of a 38.5 perch allotment of private land at Hill Street, Dehiwala by deed of transfer for Rs. 240,000,000 is a transfer of title of land situated in Sri Lanka and so falls within section 2(1)(a).

No section 3(1) exemption is available to him: he is not a diplomatic mission or international organisation, not a dual citizen, not the next of kin of the owner, and not a bank or finance leasing institution, and the subject land is bare land over which no condominium plan has been registered, so there is no condominium parcel for him to purchase.

His proposal to remit the entire price of Rs. 240,000,000 from Stockholm before execution does not save the transaction, because the inward remittance condition attaches only to the condominium parcel exemption and not to a purchase of bare land.
He cannot rely on the Ministerial exemption either, because he holds no Order made with Cabinet approval and his private apartment venture has not been identified as a Strategic Development Project.
A deed of transfer to him executed in October 2024 would therefore be void, and the Registrar of Lands would be bound to refuse its registration, leaving him with no title for the price he pays.

Since he is willing to restructure, a lease of the land to him for a term not exceeding ninety-nine years is lawful, and because the indenture would be executed well after 1 January 2016 no Land Lease Tax would be chargeable on it.

Alternatively he may acquire through a company incorporated in Sri Lanka in which his foreign shareholding is less than fifty per cent, provided he is warned that it must stay below that level for twenty consecutive years or the transfer becomes void.
On his question about construction finance, whichever of those routes he takes, the land cannot be mortgaged or pledged to a licensed bank for five years from execution of the instrument.
He must be advised that he cannot purchase this land in his own name, that a deed of transfer to him would be void and unregistrable, and that as his Notary you should decline to draw or attest it.

He should be advised to proceed instead by a lease not exceeding ninety-nine years, or through a Sri Lankan company with foreign shareholding kept below fifty per cent for twenty years, or, if his object is completed apartments, by purchasing registered condominium parcels with the entire value remitted from abroad before execution.

enrichment.original_background: A foreigner wishes to purchase a land in Sri Lanka for his Apartment business. You have been retained by him as his Attorney-at-Law and Notary.
enrichment.enriched_background:
Mr. Anders Holmqvist, a citizen of Sweden holding a Swedish passport, wishes to purchase a land in Sri Lanka for his apartment business. He has never been a citizen of Sri Lanka, has not obtained dual citizenship, and is in Sri Lanka on a resident visa. You have been retained by him as his Attorney-at-Law and Notary.

The property he has selected is Lot 4 in Survey Plan No. 8172 dated 12 March 2019 made by K. A. Weerasooriya, Licensed Surveyor, an allotment of bare private land 38.5 perches in extent called 'Nelumwatta', bearing assessment No. 118/3, Hill Street, Dehiwala, in the District of Colombo, Western Province. It is held in freehold by Mrs. S. P. Dharmasiri, a citizen of Sri Lanka, who is willing to sell. The land is bare, with no building on it and no condominium plan of any kind registered over it. Mr. Holmqvist intends to construct a twelve-storey residential apartment building on it and to sell and rent out the apartments. The agreed price is Rs. 240,000,000, which he proposes to remit in full from his bank in Stockholm to a Sri Lankan bank before the deed is executed.

He instructs you on 2 September 2024 and wishes the deed of transfer to be drawn, executed and attested in October 2024. He also asks whether he can mortgage the property to a local bank to fund construction. He has not incorporated any company in Sri Lanka. He is not related to the owner, holds no approval of the Cabinet of Ministers and no project approval of any kind, is not a diplomatic mission or an international organisation, and is not a bank or a finance leasing institution. He tells you he is willing to restructure the transaction if that is what the law requires.

added_facts.fact: The client is Mr. Anders Holmqvist, a citizen of Sweden holding a Swedish passport. He has never been a citizen of Sri Lanka, has not obtained dual citizenship, and is in Sri Lanka on a resident visa.
added_facts.reason: The question says only 'a foreigner'. The prohibition operates on a defined term that turns solely on the absence of Sri Lankan citizenship, and one of the statutory exemptions is for dual citizens, so the client's citizenship status has to be pinned down before the answer is determinate.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: Had he held dual Sri Lankan citizenship, the prohibition would not apply to him at all and the advice would be that he may take title outright.

added_facts.fact: The property he has selected is Lot 4 in Survey Plan No. 8172 dated 12 March 2019 made by K. A. Weerasooriya, Licensed Surveyor, an allotment of bare private land 38.5 perches in extent called 'Nelumwatta', bearing assessment No. 118/3, Hill Street, Dehiwala, in the District of Colombo, Western Province. It is held in freehold by Mrs. S. P. Dharmasiri, a citizen of Sri Lanka, who is willing to sell.
added_facts.reason: The question does not identify the land. The Act applies to land situated in Sri Lanka, distinguishes State from private land, and treats a condominium parcel differently from bare land, so the identity, location and character of the land are needed.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: Had the land been State land taken on lease, the re-vesting and sub-letting controls in section 5 would also have been engaged; had it been land outside Sri Lanka, the Act would not apply.

added_facts.fact: The land is bare land with no building on it and no condominium plan of any kind registered over it. Mr. Holmqvist intends to construct a twelve-storey residential apartment building on it and to sell and rent out the apartments.
added_facts.reason: 'Apartment business' is ambiguous between buying finished apartments and buying land on which to develop them. Only the first can fall within the condominium exemption, so the distinction decides the outcome.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: Had he been buying an already registered condominium parcel and remitting the entire value from abroad before execution, the exemption would apply and he could take title in his own name.

added_facts.fact: The agreed price is Rs. 240,000,000, which he proposes to remit in full from his bank in Stockholm to a Sri Lankan bank before the deed is executed.
added_facts.reason: Supplies the missing consideration and shows that the mode of payment is an inward foreign remittance, which is a condition of the condominium exemption and therefore has to appear on the facts so that it can be ruled out as a cure.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: None on the outcome: an inward remittance of the full price does not cure a purchase of bare land, because the exemption it belongs to is confined to condominium parcels.

added_facts.fact: He instructs you on 2 September 2024 and wishes the deed of transfer to be drawn, executed and attested in October 2024. He also asks whether he can mortgage the property to a local bank to fund construction.
added_facts.reason: Fixes the time of the transaction, which the question leaves open, so that the version of the statute in force can be identified, and raises the funding point on which the five-year mortgage bar bites.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: Had the deed been executed before 1 January 2013 the repealed Part VI regime would have governed it; had a lease been executed before 1 January 2016 the Land Lease Tax would still have been payable.

added_facts.fact: Mr. Holmqvist has not incorporated any company in Sri Lanka. He is not related to the owner, holds no approval of the Cabinet of Ministers and no project approval of any kind, is not a diplomatic mission or an international organisation, and is not a bank or a finance leasing institution. He tells you he is willing to restructure the transaction if that is what the law requires.
added_facts.reason: Closes off, on the facts, every exemption in the Act, so that the conclusion that the prohibition applies is determinate rather than merely probable, and opens the corporate and lease alternatives.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: Had his venture been identified as a Strategic Development Project in a listed sector and exempted by Ministerial Order, or had he already held shares in a Sri Lankan company with less than fifty per cent foreign shareholding, a purchase route would have been open.

block_reason: Five answer claims are disputed. The gold answer turns the discharge or release of the subsisting mortgage bond, the examination of the vendor's earlier chain of deeds, and the obtaining of the company secretary's proof of shareholding into steps the notary must take; none of the three has a source in the frozen corpus, and the map's own corpus_gaps says non-statutory conveyancing practice was to be excluded. A lawyer must decide whether to keep those steps and reclassify the authority requirement as mixed, or to cut them and restore proposed_gold.

indispensable_provisions.relevant_excerpt: Before any deed or instrument (other than a will or codicil) affecting any interest in land or other immovable property is drawn by him, he shall search or cause to be searched the registers in the land registry to ascertain the state of the title in regard to such land and whether any prior deed affecting any interest in such land has been registered;
indispensable_provisions.why_relevant: Imposes the notary's first substantive step: a search of the land registry registers to ascertain the state of the title and prior registered deeds before the deed of transfer is drawn.
indispensable_provisions.temporal_note: Long-standing rule, not altered by the Notaries (Amendment) Acts of 2022 or 2024, so the quoted text was in force at April 2023.

indispensable_provisions.relevant_excerpt: he shall obtain from the Registrar of the relevant Land Registry the certified extract of the folio containing the last entry pertaining to such land or immovable property containing the ownership and the registered encumbrances relating to such land or immovable property;
indispensable_provisions.why_relevant: Requires the notary to obtain the certified folio extract showing ownership and registered encumbrances, which is how the search result and any subsisting mortgage is established.
indispensable_provisions.temporal_note: Rule as substituted or inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 31 of 2022; that text was in force at April 2023. The consolidated corpus text of section 31 also carries later changes made by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 6 of 2024, but this rule was not among them.

indispensable_provisions.relevant_excerpt: if a party to any deed or instrument is a corporate body he shall retain a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation or other instrument establishing such corporate entity and details of board of directors;
indispensable_provisions.why_relevant: Where the purchaser is a company, the notary must call for and retain a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation and the details of the board of directors.
indispensable_provisions.temporal_note: Rule as substituted or inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 31 of 2022; that text was in force at April 2023. The consolidated corpus text of section 31 also carries later changes made by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 6 of 2024, but this rule was not among them.

indispensable_provisions.relevant_excerpt: if an executant to any deed or instrument is a corporate body, cause to be affixed the seal of the corporate body and obtain the signatures of the board of directors or any person authorized by the board by resolution to sign such deed or instrument and if the name of such executant or witness differs from the name given in the identification documents of such executant or witness, he shall, in his attestation of such deed or instrument, describe such executant or witness by such name and by the name written in the signature.
indispensable_provisions.why_relevant: Governs how a corporate executant signs: the notary must cause the seal of the corporate body to be affixed and obtain the signatures of the board or of a person authorised by board resolution.
indispensable_provisions.temporal_note: Rule as substituted or inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 31 of 2022; that text was in force at April 2023. The consolidated corpus text of section 31 also carries later changes made by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 6 of 2024, but this rule was not among them.

indispensable_provisions.relevant_excerpt: Where the executant is a body corporate, he shall attach a copy of the board resolution authorizing the executant to sign such deed or instrument to the protocol of such deed or instrument.
